lessons.title: Record Date, Entitlement Ratio, and the Special Pre-Open Session

children.text: On 19 July 2023, Reliance Industries closed at ₹2,841.85. The next morning, before normal trading began, it was priced at ₹2,580. Plenty of first-time investors saw a fall of ₹261.85 on their Zerodha app and assumed something had gone badly wrong. Nothing had. That morning was the record date for the Jio Financial Services demerger, and ₹261.85 was the value the market assigned to the JFS share each of them was about to receive. The mechanics of that single day decide who gets the new shares, what price the parent opens at, and why your holdings screen looks strange for weeks afterwards.

body.text: On the record date, value moves, it does not disappear. The parent's price drops by roughly the value of the business carved out, and that value reappears as new shares in your demat account. Judge a demerger by adding both holdings together, never by the parent's price alone.

children.text: The Entitlement Ratio
The scheme of arrangement fixes an
entitlement ratio

: how many shares of the resulting company you receive for the parent shares you hold. Unlike a merger's swap ratio, nothing is cancelled. You keep every parent share and receive the new shares on top.

markDefs.definition: In a demerger, the number of resulting company shares issued for a stated number of parent company shares held on the record date.

body.caption: Entitlement ratios in recent Indian demergers

cells: Jio Financial Services from Reliance Industries (2023)
1 JFS share for every 1 Reliance share
1 ITC Hotels share for every 10 ITC shares
1 Sahyadri Hotels share for every 5 Sahyadri shares

body.text: The ratio only decides how the carved-out value is packaged. A 1 for 10 ratio gives you fewer, higher-priced new shares, and a 1 for 1 ratio gives you more, lower-priced ones. The rupee value you receive depends on the business transferred, not on the ratio.

children.text: The Record Date: Who Gets the New Shares
After the scheme becomes effective, the parent announces a
record date
. Anyone whose name appears in the depository records as a shareholder at the end of that day receives the new shares. Since Indian equity markets moved to T+1 settlement in January 2023, the
ex-date
and the record date fall on the same day.

markDefs.definition: The date on which a company checks its register of members and beneficial owners with NSDL and CDSL to decide who is entitled to a corporate action such as demerger shares, a dividend or a bonus issue.
The first trading day on which a share trades without the right to the corporate action. Buying on or after the ex-date does not entitle you to it.

body.latex: \text{Last day to buy and still be entitled} = \text{Trading day before the record date}
body.caption: Under T+1 settlement, shares bought on a trading day reach your demat account the next trading day, so a purchase on the day before the record date settles on the record date itself.

body.title: Who is entitled?
body.question: Sahyadri Industries fixes Friday as the record date for its hotels demerger. Four investors trade Sahyadri shares that week. Which statement is correct?
options: Asha, who buys on Friday morning, receives Sahyadri Hotels shares because she owns Sahyadri on the record date
Bharat, who buys on Thursday and sells on Friday, receives Sahyadri Hotels shares
Chetan, who sells on Thursday, still receives Sahyadri Hotels shares because he owned Sahyadri earlier in the week
Divya, who buys on Friday and sells the following Monday, receives Sahyadri Hotels shares
body.explanation: Bharat's Thursday purchase settles on Friday, so he is on record at the end of the record date. His Friday sale settles on Monday, after the record date, so it does not affect his entitlement. Asha and Divya bought on the ex-date, and their purchases settle only on Monday, too late. Chetan's Thursday sale settles on Friday, so he is no longer a shareholder on the record date.

children.text: The Special Pre-Open Session: Finding the Parent's New Price

On the record date, the parent is suddenly a smaller company, but the previous day's closing price still reflects the whole business. Instead of leaving the price to jump around in normal trading, NSE and BSE hold a
special pre-open session
for the parent's shares before regular trading begins. Buy and sell orders are collected and matched in a call auction to discover a fair opening price for the parent without the demerged business.

markDefs.definition: A call auction held for a stock on the ex-date of a demerger, before normal trading starts, in which orders are collected and a single equilibrium price is discovered for the parent after the carved-out business has left.

body.latex: \text{Implied value carved out per parent share} = \text{Previous close} - \text{Price discovered in special session}
body.caption: This difference is widely used as the notional value of the resulting company until its shares list.

body.label: Reliance Industries special pre-open session, 20 July 2023
body.context: With a 1 for 1 entitlement ratio, ₹261.85 became the implied value of each Jio Financial Services share until JFS listed a month later.

children.text: Worked Example: Sahyadri Hotels at 1 for 5

Sahyadri Industries closes at ₹290 on the day before the record date. In the special pre-open session, the price is discovered at ₹262. The entitlement ratio is 1 Sahyadri Hotels share for every 5 Sahyadri shares.

body.title: Implied value of one new share
body.prompt: What is the implied value of one Sahyadri Hotels share, in rupees? Remember that 5 Sahyadri shares produce 1 Sahyadri Hotels share.
body.explanation: Value carved out per Sahyadri share = ₹290 minus ₹262 = ₹28. It takes 5 Sahyadri shares to receive 1 Sahyadri Hotels share, so one Sahyadri Hotels share is implicitly worth ₹28 × 5 = ₹140. With a 1 for 1 ratio, as with Reliance and JFS, the two numbers are the same. With any other ratio, you must adjust.

body.title: Check your portfolio
body.prompt: Pooja holds 500 Sahyadri shares. Using the implied value of ₹140 per Sahyadri Hotels share and the discovered Sahyadri price of ₹262, what is the combined value of her holdings immediately after the record date, in rupees?
body.explanation: Sahyadri: 500 × ₹262 = ₹1,31,000. Sahyadri Hotels: 500 ÷ 5 = 100 shares × ₹140 = ₹14,000. Total = ₹1,45,000, exactly her 500 × ₹290 = ₹1,45,000 from the previous evening. The demerger itself did not change her wealth.

body.title: Pooja's holdings before and after the record date (₹)

body.text: The implied value is not a guaranteed listing price. It is what the special session implied about the parent, not a trade in the new company's shares. When the resulting company actually lists weeks later, its price can land well above or below the implied value.

children.text: The Weeks Between Record Date and Listing

body.title: What happens after the record date

events.title: Special pre-open session and ex-date trading
events.description: The parent's new price is discovered and it trades normally for the rest of the day without the demerged business.

events.date: Days to a few weeks later
events.title: New shares credited to demat accounts
events.description: The resulting company allots shares and NSDL and CDSL credit them. Your broker may show them with no price, or at zero value.

events.title: Listing approvals
events.description: The resulting company applies to the stock exchanges and seeks the regulatory relaxation needed to list without an IPO.

events.title: New shares start trading
events.description: Price discovery happens again, this time in the new company's own shares. Jio Financial Services listed on 21 August 2023, and ITC Hotels on 29 January 2025.

body.title: Your new shares before and after listing

columns.label: Credited but not yet listed
points: Visible in your demat account and broker holdings
Cannot be sold on NSE or BSE
Often shown at zero or no price in apps such as Kite
Cost of acquisition usually blank or zero until you update it

columns.label: After listing
points: Trades normally and can be sold
Market price replaces the implied value
Price can swing sharply in the first days as investors reposition
Index funds may have to sell if the stock does not qualify for their index
Update your cost split before selling, as Lesson 4.3 explains

body.title: Why index funds matter in the first days after listing

children.text: When a Nifty 50 or Sensex company demerges a business, index funds and ETFs tracking that index receive the new shares like everyone else. To avoid disrupting these funds, index providers have typically added the resulting company to the index temporarily at its implied value, then removed it after it lists.

Once the new company is removed, passive funds that do not track any index containing it must sell. That selling is mechanical and has nothing to do with the business. After Jio Financial Services listed in August 2023, it hit its lower circuit on the first days of trading, a period when index-related selling was widely cited. Knowing this can stop you from panic-selling a new stock for the wrong reason.

If you trade futures or options in the parent, the exchanges also adjust open contracts, typically changing strike prices and lot sizes by an adjustment factor based on the special session, so that the demerger does not create artificial gains or losses in derivatives.

body.title: The key date
body.textWithBlank: To receive demerger shares, you must be a shareholder in the depository records at the end of the ___ date.
body.explanation: The record date decides entitlement. Under T+1 settlement, that means buying no later than the trading day before it.

body.title: The missing ₹28 per share
body.scenario: Your uncle holds 2,000 Sahyadri Industries shares. On the record date, he calls you in a panic: his Kite app shows Sahyadri down from ₹290 to ₹262, a loss of ₹56,000, and he cannot find any Sahyadri Hotels shares. He wants to sell everything before it falls further.
body.prompt: What would you explain to him, and what should he actually do?
body.modelAnswer:
1. No loss has happened. The ₹28 per share fall is the value of the hotels business leaving Sahyadri. At 1 for 5, he is entitled to 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400 Sahyadri Hotels shares, implicitly worth 400 × ₹140 = ₹56,000, exactly the amount that seems missing.
2. The new shares take time to appear. They are credited to his demat account days or weeks after the record date and cannot be sold until the company lists.
3. When they show up, they may display at zero value. That is a display issue, not the actual worth.
4. Selling Sahyadri today would not undo anything. He would still receive the Sahyadri Hotels shares, because he was on record, and he would just be exiting the parent at ₹262.
5. What to do: note the special session price and implied value for his records, wait for the credit and listing, then update the cost split between the two holdings using the company's announcement, as Lesson 4.3 shows.
6. Decide on each business separately once both are trading, instead of reacting on the record date.

body.title: Demerger record date checklist
steps: Note the entitlement ratio and the record date from the company's exchange filing
If buying for the entitlement, complete the purchase by the trading day before the record date
Record the parent's previous close and its special session price
Calculate the implied value per new share, adjusting for the ratio
Confirm the new shares are credited to your demat account
Wait for listing before expecting to trade them, and update your cost of acquisition split

body.label: NSE India
body.description: Search the parent company and open its corporate actions and announcements to find the record date, entitlement ratio and special pre-open session notice.

cards.definition: The number of resulting company shares received for a stated number of parent shares held.
The date on which depository records decide who is entitled to a corporate action.
The first day a share trades without the right to the corporate action. Under T+1, it is the same as the record date.
A call auction on the ex-date of a demerger to discover the parent's price without the demerged business.
Previous close minus the special session price, adjusted for the entitlement ratio to get a value per new share.
The day the resulting company's shares begin trading, often weeks after the record date.

points: The entitlement ratio decides how many new shares you receive, and you keep all your parent shares.
Under T+1 settlement, buy by the trading day before the record date to be entitled. Selling on the record date does not remove your entitlement.
A special pre-open session on the record date discovers the parent's price without the demerged business.
Previous close minus the special session price gives the value carved out per parent share: ₹261.85 for each JFS share in 2023.
Adjust for the ratio: at 1 for 5, a ₹28 drop in the parent implies ₹140 per new share.
New shares take weeks to list, may show at zero value until then, and can swing sharply after listing, partly because of index fund selling.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment, tax or legal advice. Sahyadri Industries, Sahyadri Hotels and the investors in the examples are fictional. Details for Reliance Industries, Jio Financial Services and ITC Hotels are from public disclosures. Exchange procedures for special sessions and index treatment can change, so check the latest exchange circulars for any specific demerger.
